summary.headline: Asian Paints Q2 FY27: decorative volume grew 6.4% and value 14.5%, while gross margin dipped to 41-43% band guidance and PBT margin fell to ~4.8% on inflation lag.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 volume growth held at about 6.4% on a high base (~11% like-for-like last year) despite two steep price hikes in Q1 and Q2. Decorative value grew 14.5%, and decorative plus industrial value grew about 16.4% with 6.8% volume. Margins were squeezed: standalone PBDIT margin fell to about 17.1% from 18.5% like-for-like, and the gross margin dipped below the 44-45% range as inflation of about 3% outran price increases of about 7% in Q1 and about 5% in Q2. Management pointed to H1 as the more representative period, with H1 standalone PBDIT margin at 19.6% and consolidated at 18.2%.

financial_highlights.metric: H1 consolidated PBDIT margin / PAT growth

segments.name: Decorative (India)
segments.commentary: Volume ~6.4% and value ~14.5% in Q2; H1 volume ~8% and value ~16%. Rural outgrowing urban; Bath, Kitchen and Weatherseal grew well, White Teak slower. New products are ~18% of revenue.

segments.name: Industrial JV1 (PPG AP, auto OE and refinish)
segments.commentary: Revenue growth about 34% in Q2; PBT up about 10% but margin fell about 309 bps to about 14.2% on inflation and price-increase lag.

segments.name: Industrial JV2 (APPPG, general industrial, protective and powder)
segments.commentary: Revenue growth about 28% in Q2; bottom line set back as price increases came with a delay, with recovery expected in Q3.

segments.name: International / AP Global
segments.commentary: Q2 growth about 30% and H1 about 28%, across Asia, Africa and Middle East. PBT margin fell to about 4.8% on inflation; Middle East and Africa more difficult than Asia.

guidance_outlook: Gross margin band of about 41% to 43% is the expected range, depending on inflation.
Further price increase of about 3.5% announced for November, covering anti-dumping duty impact and cost inflation.
Management expects to maintain the EBITDA margin band of 18% to 20% for FY27, supported by pricing, cost excellence and VAE.
Volume growth of about 8% to 9% expected going forward, helped by a longer Diwali in November and the wedding season, with rural demand a question given monsoon deficit.
International PBT margin expected to recover in Q3 and Q4 as staggered price increases flow through.
Anti-dumping duty on TiO2 effective from 24th October; impact estimated at 2% to 3% of cost.
capex_capacity: GenNext VAE (vinyl acetate ethylene) emulsion plant: phase 1 commissioned in September 2026 out of total capex of about Rs. 3,250 crore; full capacity of 150 KT targeted within about a year (next year).
Phase 1 to be partially utilised through March; full utilisation of phase 1 expected in the next year.
VAE benefit estimated at 300 bps to 500 bps on relevant products at full potential; partial benefit in phase 1 and full benefit as phase 2 progresses.
Cost excellence programme launched to offset part of inflation.
demand_pricing: Price hikes of about 7% in Q1 and about 5% in Q2 against cost inflation of about 28% cited by the analyst (cost inflation ~3% in Q2 per management), so pricing did not fully cover inflation.
Competitive intensity at network level, including promotions, has risen; competitors are following similar pricing trajectory.
Q2 product mix was seasonal and weaker, with no exterior sales in the quarter, which affected margins; Q3 expected to bring better mix.
Management prefers calibrated pricing to avoid disrupting demand, and says it will not pass on the full inflation at present.
Industrial pricing lags are typical of B2B; JV2 saw a greater lag than JV1.

qa_highlights.question: How is demand shaping up and has the inventory filled in Q1 normalised; what is October volume trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the full inventory impact was borne in Q2; Q2 is a stocking quarter with seasonal mix, and 7% volume growth is considered decent.

qa_highlights.question: What normalised gross margin should be expected in H2 as exterior sales return and pricing is taken?
qa_highlights.answer: A gross margin band of about 41% to 43% is the target range, depending on inflation; a further ~3.5% price increase is announced for November.

qa_highlights.question: Do the 18% to 20% EBITDA margin band and VAE/cost savings remain achievable?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 margins at standalone and consolidated levels are within the band and the company expects to maintain 18% to 20% for the year, backed by cost excellence and VAE.

qa_highlights.question: What is the VAE benefit and is it available to competitors?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is a differentiated VAE, not generic; benefit of 300 bps to 500 bps on relevant products at full potential, with partial benefit in phase 1.

qa_highlights.question: How will the industrial and international margin lags be recovered, and can TiO2 anti-dumping costs be passed through?
qa_highlights.answer: Industrial pricing lags as B2B; JV2 lag greater. International Middle East and Africa more difficult. ADD on TiO2 impact of 2% to 3% of cost, mitigated by lower TiO2 usage and grade mix.

qa_highlights.question: Is the industry able to pass on input inflation, and what is the outlook for volumes?
qa_highlights.answer: Competitors are on similar pricing, promotional intensity has gone up, and full pass-through is not reasonable currently. Volume growth of about 8% to 9% expected going forward.

risks_watch: Gross margin and PBT margin trajectory against the 41-43% gross margin band and 18-20% EBITDA margin band in H2.
Raw material and TiO2 inflation, with anti-dumping duty effective 24 October and China pricing as a key variable.
Price elasticity and down-trading risk in a discretionary category; competitive promotional intensity.
Rural demand softness due to monsoon deficit; Middle East and Africa geopolitical exposure in international business.
Delivery of VAE phase 1 full capacity and realisation of the 300-500 bps benefit within the next year.
Industrial JV margin recovery as delayed price increases take effect in Q3.
summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line and volume resilience and on H1 margins, but cautious on Q2 profitability, inflation pass-through and the outlook given volatility and anti-dumping duty. Management was reluctant to say full cost pass-through is achievable now and framed Q2 as a seasonal, atypical quarter.
key_quotes: So, the overall volumes despite a very high inflationary environment and the steep price hikes which have been taken, both in quarter one and quarter two, we have been able to grow at a good volume of about 6.4%.
So, I would say that this multitude of factors is something which is all in the consideration which we make so that possibly we can assuage some of the apprehensions of the customer level.
We believe as we go forward, for the year we should be able to maintain the band of what we have spoken of 18% to 20%.
And as I said, with the full capacity of 150 KT we should be able to utilize in the next year.

adds.what: GenNext VAE emulsion plant, 150 KT full capacity (phase 1 commissioned Sep 2026)

growth.why: Management guides volume growth of about 8-9% for H2 FY27 and reaffirms an 18-20% EBITDA margin band for FY27, backed partly by the VAE emulsion plant (phase 1 commissioned Sep 2026, full 150 KT within about a year), pricing and cost actions, with the order book and demand not quantified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Management holds the 18-20% EBITDA margin band for FY27 (H1 standalone PBDIT 19.6%, consolidated 18.2%) and expects a better Q3 mix; gross margin guided to 41-43% after a further ~3.5% November price hike, with the VAE benefit of 300-500 bps only partial in phase 1, so Q2 PBDIT margin of 17.1% (vs 18.5%) shows the lag is not yet closed.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: GenNext VAE emulsion plant phase 1 was commissioned in September 2026 out of ~Rs. 3,250 crore total capex, with full 150 KT capacity targeted within about a year; ramp-up is already under way and partially utilised through March.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides volume growth of about 8-9% going forward, helped by a longer Diwali and wedding season, after H1 decorative volume of ~8% and Q2 volume of ~6.4% on a ~11% base; rural demand is a question given the monsoon deficit.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Management's commentary centres on ramping the newly commissioned VAE plant to full capacity within a year, with no new capacity or capex plan discussed; the call does not quantify utilisation, so no near-term announcement is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Guidance was held (volume 8-9%, EBITDA margin 18-20%, gross margin 41-43%) with management cautious on pass-through and anti-dumping duty impact of 2-3% of cost, so a raise is not signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Q2 PBDIT margin fell to 17.1% and consolidated margin to 15.6% (down ~202 bps), inflation (~3% in Q2 per management) outran price hikes of ~7% and ~5%, and TiO2 anti-dumping duty adds 2-3% of cost from 24 October, while competitive promotions are rising and international PBT margin fell to ~4.8%.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: New products are already ~18% of decorative revenue and the VAE-based differentiated emulsion range is coming on stream, but the call gives no named product launch dates.

rows.label: Further ~3.5% price hike in November
rows.why: Management has announced a ~3.5% price increase for November covering anti-dumping duty and cost inflation, following ~7% in Q1 and ~5% in Q2.

rows.label: International margin recovery in Q3-Q4
rows.why: Management expects International PBT margin, currently ~4.8% after Q2 inflation, to recover as staggered price increases flow through; International grew ~30% in Q2 and ~28% in H1.

rows.label: Industrial JV2 margin recovery
rows.why: JV2 price increases came with a delay and recovery is expected in Q3; JV1 PBT margin already fell ~309 bps to ~14.2% on the same lag, while revenue grew ~34% and ~28% respectively.

tone.note: Management was confident on volume resilience (Q2 ~6.4%, H1 ~8%), the 18-20% EBITDA band and VAE benefit, but cautious on Q2 margins, pass-through of inflation and anti-dumping duty; analysts pressed on gross margin recovery, industrial and international lags and whether competitors can pass on cost
